problems.title: Two Sum
problems.key_insight: Store each value's index in a dict; for each x, check whether target - x was already seen. One pass.
problems.statement: Return the indices of the two numbers in an array that add up to a target. Exactly one answer exists.
edge_cases: The same value twice, e.g. [3, 3] with target 6
problems.google_follow_up: What if the array is sorted? Can you do it with O(1) extra space?

problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.key_insight: Add values to a set one by one; a value that is already in the set is a duplicate.
problems.statement: Return true if any value appears at least twice in the array.
problems.google_follow_up: What if you must use O(1) extra space? What does sorting cost you?

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.key_insight: Two strings are anagrams exactly when their letter counts match: Counter(s) == Counter(t).
problems.statement: Return true if t is an anagram of s: the same letters with the same counts, in any order.
problems.google_follow_up: What if the input can hold any Unicode character, not just a-z?

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.key_pattern: Hash map with a canonical key
problems.key_insight: Anagrams share the same sorted string (or the same 26-letter count tuple); use it as the dict key.
problems.statement: Group the strings that are anagrams of each other.
problems.google_follow_up: The strings are very long: how do you avoid sorting each one?

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.key_insight: answer[i] = product of everything left of i times everything right of i; build both in two passes, no division.
problems.statement: Return an array where each element is the product of all the other elements, without using division.
problems.google_follow_up: Can you do it with O(1) extra space besides the output array?

problems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.key_pattern: Hash set, count only from run starts
problems.key_insight: Put the numbers in a set; start counting at x only when x - 1 is missing, so each number is visited O(1) times.
problems.statement: Return the length of the longest run of consecutive integers in an unsorted array, in O(n) time.
problems.google_follow_up: The numbers arrive as a stream. How do you keep the longest run up to date?

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.key_insight: Move a left and a right pointer inward, skip characters that are not letters or digits, compare lower-cased characters.
problems.statement: After lower-casing and removing non-alphanumeric characters, does the string read the same forwards and backwards?
problems.google_follow_up: What if you may delete at most one character (Valid Palindrome II)?

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
problems.key_insight: A write pointer marks where the next new value goes; a read pointer scans; copy only when the value changes.
problems.statement: Remove duplicates in place from a sorted array and return the number of unique values.
problems.google_follow_up: Allow each value at most twice (Remove Duplicates II). What changes?

problems.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
problems.key_pattern: Two pointers on a sorted array
problems.key_insight: Start at both ends: if the sum is too small move the left pointer up, if too big move the right pointer down.
problems.statement: In a sorted array, return the 1-based indices of the two numbers that add up to target, using O(1) extra space.
problems.google_follow_up: How does the same idea extend to 3Sum?

problems.title: 3Sum
problems.key_insight: Sort, fix one number, then run the sorted Two Sum with two pointers on the rest; skip equal values to avoid repeated triplets.
problems.space_target: O(1) besides sorting and the output
problems.statement: Return all unique triplets in the array that sum to zero.
problems.google_follow_up: How do you generalise this to kSum?

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.key_pattern: Two pointers, move the shorter side
problems.key_insight: The area is limited by the shorter line; moving the taller line can never help, so always move the shorter one inward.
problems.statement: Pick two lines from a height array that hold the most water between them; return that area.
problems.google_follow_up: Why is it safe to throw away the shorter line? Prove it.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.key_insight: Track the lowest price so far; on each day the best sale is price - lowest so far.
problems.statement: Given daily prices, return the maximum profit from one buy followed by one later sell (0 if no profit is possible).
problems.google_follow_up: What if you can buy and sell many times (Stock II)?

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.key_pattern: Sliding window with a last-seen map
problems.key_insight: Grow the window to the right; when a character repeats, move the left edge past its previous position (never backwards).
problems.statement: Return the length of the longest substring that has no repeated characters.
problems.google_follow_up: What if at most k distinct characters are allowed instead?

problems.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
problems.key_insight: A window is fine when its length minus the count of its most common letter is at most k; shrink from the left when it is not.
problems.statement: You may change up to k characters. Return the length of the longest substring that can be made of one repeated letter.
edge_cases: k is at least the string length
problems.google_follow_up: Why is it safe to never lower the stored maximum count?

problems.title: Permutation in String
problems.key_insight: Slide a window of len(s1) over s2 and compare letter counts; update the counts in O(1) per step.
problems.statement: Return true if some substring of s2 is a permutation of s1.
problems.google_follow_up: Return every starting index instead (Find All Anagrams in a String).

problems.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
problems.key_insight: If prefix[j] - prefix[i] == k, the part between them sums to k; count earlier prefix sums equal to current - k.
problems.statement: Count the contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k. Values can be negative.
problems.google_follow_up: Why does a sliding window fail here but work when all numbers are positive?

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.key_pattern: Binary search on a sorted array
problems.key_insight: Keep lo..hi as the range that may still hold the target; halve it each step and stop when lo > hi.
problems.statement: Return the index of target in a sorted array, or -1 if it is missing.
edge_cases: Target smaller or bigger than every element
problems.google_follow_up: Return the first position where target could be inserted instead (like bisect_left).

problems.title: Search Insert Position
problems.key_insight: Find the first index whose value is >= target; that is both the match and the insert position.
problems.statement: Return the index of target in a sorted array, or the index where it would be inserted.
problems.google_follow_up: How do you find the last position of a repeated value instead?

problems.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.key_pattern: Binary search: pick the sorted half
problems.key_insight: At each mid one half is sorted; check whether target lies inside that half's range and keep the matching side.
problems.statement: A sorted array of distinct values was rotated at an unknown point. Find target's index in O(log n), or return -1.
problems.google_follow_up: What if duplicates are allowed? What is the worst case then?

problems.title: Koko Eating Bananas
problems.key_insight: If speed s is fast enough, every faster speed is too; binary-search the smallest speed that finishes within h hours.
problems.statement: Find the minimum eating speed k so all banana piles are finished within h hours, eating from at most one pile per hour.
edge_cases: h equals the number of piles
problems.google_follow_up: Name two other problems where you binary-search the answer, not the array.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.key_insight: Walk the list once, pointing each node back at the previous one; save the next node before you overwrite the link.
problems.statement: Reverse a singly linked list and return the new head.
problems.google_follow_up: Reverse only the part between positions left and right (Reverse Linked List II).

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.key_insight: Use a dummy node and always attach the smaller head; attach whatever is left of the other list at the end.
problems.statement: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
problems.google_follow_up: Merge k sorted lists. What is the complexity with a heap?

problems.title: Linked List Cycle
problems.key_insight: Move slow by 1 and fast by 2; they meet if and only if the list has a cycle.
problems.statement: Return true if a linked list has a cycle, using O(1) memory.
edge_cases: The cycle goes back to the head
problems.google_follow_up: Return the node where the cycle starts (Linked List Cycle II).

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
problems.key_insight: Move fast n steps ahead, then move both until fast reaches the end; slow is just before the node to remove (start from a dummy).
problems.statement: Remove the n-th node from the end of a linked list and return its head.
edge_cases: Remove the head (n equals the length)
problems.google_follow_up: Can you do it in one pass, without first counting the length?

problems.title: Reorder List
problems.key_insight: Split at the middle with slow/fast pointers, reverse the second half, then weave the two halves together.
problems.statement: Reorder L0, L1, ..., Ln into L0, Ln, L1, Ln-1, ... in place.
problems.google_follow_up: This combines three linked-list skills. Which step usually breaks, and how do you test it?

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.key_insight: Push opening brackets; each closing bracket must match the top of the stack; the stack must end empty.
problems.statement: Return true if the brackets ()[]{} in the string are correctly matched and nested.
problems.google_follow_up: What is the minimum number of brackets you must add to make it valid?

problems.title: Min Stack
problems.key_insight: Store the current minimum next to every pushed value, so getMin is just the stored minimum on top.
problems.statement: Design a stack with push, pop, top and getMin, each in O(1) time.
problems.google_follow_up: Can you save memory by storing the minimum only when it changes?

problems.title: LRU Cache
problems.key_insight: The dict gives O(1) lookup; the linked list keeps the use order, so the least recently used key is evicted from the front in O(1).
problems.statement: Design a cache with get and put in O(1) that evicts the least recently used key when it is full.
edge_cases: put on an existing key updates its value and makes it most recent
problems.google_follow_up: How would you make it safe when many threads call it at once?

drills.prompt: Return the indices of the two numbers in an array that add up to a target. Exactly one answer exists.
drills.pattern: Hash map of seen values: Store each value's index in a dict; for each x, check whether target - x was already seen. One pass.
drills.edge_case: The same value twice, e.g. [3, 3] with target 6

drills.prompt: Return the length of the longest run of consecutive integers in an unsorted array, in O(n) time.
drills.pattern: Hash set, count only from run starts: Put the numbers in a set; start counting at x only when x - 1 is missing, so each number is visited O(1) times.

drills.prompt: Return all unique triplets in the array that sum to zero.
drills.pattern: Sort, then two pointers: Sort, fix one number, then run the sorted Two Sum with two pointers on the rest; skip equal values to avoid repeated triplets.
drills.complexity: O(n^2) time, O(1) besides sorting and the output space

drills.prompt: Pick two lines from a height array that hold the most water between them; return that area.
drills.pattern: Two pointers, move the shorter side: The area is limited by the shorter line; moving the taller line can never help, so always move the shorter one inward.

drills.prompt: Return the length of the longest substring that has no repeated characters.
drills.pattern: Sliding window with a last-seen map: Grow the window to the right; when a character repeats, move the left edge past its previous position (never backwards).

drills.prompt: Count the contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k. Values can be negative.
drills.pattern: Prefix sums + hash map: If prefix[j] - prefix[i] == k, the part between them sums to k; count earlier prefix sums equal to current - k.

drills.prompt: A sorted array of distinct values was rotated at an unknown point. Find target's index in O(log n), or return -1.
drills.pattern: Binary search: pick the sorted half: At each mid one half is sorted; check whether target lies inside that half's range and keep the matching side.

drills.prompt: Find the minimum eating speed k so all banana piles are finished within h hours, eating from at most one pile per hour.
drills.pattern: Binary search on the answer: If speed s is fast enough, every faster speed is too; binary-search the smallest speed that finishes within h hours.
drills.complexity: O(n log m) time, O(1) space
drills.edge_case: h equals the number of piles

drills.prompt: Reverse a singly linked list and return the new head.
drills.pattern: Pointer reversal (prev, cur): Walk the list once, pointing each node back at the previous one; save the next node before you overwrite the link.

drills.prompt: Return true if a linked list has a cycle, using O(1) memory.
drills.pattern: Fast and slow pointers: Move slow by 1 and fast by 2; they meet if and only if the list has a cycle.

drills.prompt: Return true if the brackets ()[]{} in the string are correctly matched and nested.
drills.pattern: Stack of open brackets: Push opening brackets; each closing bracket must match the top of the stack; the stack must end empty.

drills.prompt: Design a cache with get and put in O(1) that evicts the least recently used key when it is full.
drills.pattern: Hash map + doubly linked list (OrderedDict): The dict gives O(1) lookup; the linked list keeps the use order, so the least recently used key is evicted from the front in O(1).
drills.complexity: O(1) per operation time, O(capacity) space

drills.pattern: 'while lo < hi' stops before checking the last candidate. With hi = len(nums) - 1 the loop must be 'while lo <= hi'.
The left edge can jump backwards to an old copy of a letter. Use left = max(left, seen[ch] + 1).

drills.prompt:
Reverse a linked list:

  prev, cur = None, head
  while cur:
      cur.next = prev
      prev = cur
      cur = cur.next
  return prev
drills.pattern: cur.next is overwritten before it is saved, so 'cur = cur.next' jumps back to prev. Save nxt = cur.next first.
drills.edge_case: Any list with 2 or more nodes stops after the first node.
